title: ECM Protein Nanofibers and Nanostructures Engineered Using Surface-initiated Assembly
protocol: Design ECM protein nanofibers, nanofabrics, and nanostructures using CAD software.
Transfer the design to a photomask suitable for feature sizes down to ~10 μm.
Dehydrate a 4" silicon wafer on a hotplate set to 150 °C for 15 min.
Center the wafer on the vacuum chuck of a spin-coater.
Pour SU8-2015 negative photoresist onto the middle of the wafer in concentric circles until about two thirds of the wafer is covered.
Program the spin-coater with a spread cycle at 500 rpm and an acceleration of 100 rpm/sec for 10 sec.
Spin the wafer cycle at 4,000 rpm with an acceleration of 100 rpm/sec for 30 sec.
Soft bake the wafer by placing it on a hotplate set to 95 °C for 3 min.
Expose the wafer with UV light through the photomask for a total dosage of 140 mJ/cm².
Post exposure bake the wafer by placing it on a hotplate set to 95 °C for 4 min.
Develop the wafer by placing it in SU8 developer for 3 min.
Rinse the wafer with isopropyl alcohol.
If a white film forms during rinsing, place the wafer back in the developer for another 30 sec and rinse again with isopropyl alcohol until no white film appears.
Dry the wafer in a stream of nitrogen.
Place the dried wafer in a 150 mm petri dish to protect from dust.
Mix PDMS prepolymer at 2,000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Degas mixed PDMS at 2,000 rpm for 2 minutes.
If a mixer is unavailable, mix PDMS by hand using a 10 ml serological pipette for 10 minutes.
Place the manually mixed PDMS in a vacuum desiccator to degas for 30 minutes.
Pour PDMS prepolymer over the master mold to form a 1 cm thick layer.
Bake the PDMS at 65 °C for 4 hours or cure at room temperature for 48 hours.
Cut out regions containing patterns from cured PDMS to form stamps.
Cut a notch in one corner of the backside of the PDMS stamp to distinguish it.
Clean 25 mm diameter glass coverslips by sonication in 95% ethanol for 1 hour.
Dry cleaned coverslips at 65 °C in an oven.
Prepare PIPAAm solution by dissolving PIPAAm in 1-butanol at a concentration of 10% (w/v).
Place a glass coverslip on the vacuum chuck of the spincoater.
Pipette 200 μl of PIPAAm solution onto the coverslip to cover its entire surface.
Spincoat the covered coverslip at 6,000 rpm for 1 minute.
Clean PDMS stamps by sonication in 50% ethanol for 30 minutes.
Dry cleaned PDMS stamps under a stream of nitrogen.
Coat the patterned surface of each PDMS stamp with 200 μl of protein solution.
Incubate for 1 hr at room temperature.
Wash the PDMS stamps in distilled water to remove excess protein.
Dry thoroughly under a stream of nitrogen.
Place the PIPAAm-coated coverslips inside a closed petri dish and sterilize using UV exposure, if sterility is required.
Perform microcontact printing by placing the feature side of the PDMS stamp in contact with the PIPAAm-coated coverslip.
Tap lightly on the back of the stamps to remove air bubbles and ensure uniform contact.
Peel off the PDMS stamp from the coverslip after 5 min.
Place the patterned PIPAAm coated coverslip in a 35 mm petri dish.
Inspect the pattern fidelity using phase contrast microscopy.
Add 3 ml of 40 °C distilled water to the petri dish.
Allow the water to gradually cool.
Monitor the dissolution of the PIPAAm layer and release of ECM protein patterns using phase contrast microscopy.
Cool the water to room temperature to ensure complete release of ECM protein nanostructures.
Manipulate the released nanofibers, nanofabrics, and other nanostructures for further applications.
